user.description: This adds tools for administrators to Home Assistant's LLM APIs, covering all entities, history, devices, automations, scripts and the system log. Any LLM client an administrator connects, such as one using the Model Context Protocol Server integration, can read this data and sends it to its model provider. Known secrets are withheld, but this cannot be guaranteed for all text. Clients can only read until you allow changes. You can narrow what is exposed, and choose what can be changed, in the settings after setup.
user.title: Set up LLM Admin Tools

data.scrub_esphome_secrets: Also withhold values from ESPHome's secrets file

data_description.extra_redacted_keys: The value stored under these names is withheld, for example ap or serial. Upper case and separators are ignored.
data_description.extra_redacted_text: This exact text is removed wherever it appears, for example a hostname, a network name or an account name.
data_description.redact_location: Coordinates and altitude, on people, zones, trackers and everything else.
data_description.redact_network: Private IP addresses, MAC addresses, network names and hostnames. These often help when diagnosing problems.
data_description.redact_personal: Email addresses, user names, phone numbers and public IP addresses. A version number with four parts can look like an IP address and be hidden too.
data_description.scrub_esphome_secrets: esphome/secrets.yaml, as well as secrets.yaml, which is always used. A value needs at least 6 characters to be recognized.

data_description.assist_exposed_only: Limit the tools to what you expose under Voice assistants, instead of all entities.
data_description.excluded_areas: Hides the area, its devices, and its entities. An entity assigned to another area than its device follows its own area.
data_description.excluded_domains: Hides all entities of these domains, for example camera or person.
data_description.excluded_entities: Hides these entities everywhere, including automations and scripts themselves if you select them.
data_description.excluded_integrations: Hides the entry from the integration list, along with its devices and entities. A few entities are not linked to their integration, such as sun.sun: hide those by entity. Log lines stay visible unless you also hide the logger.
data_description.excluded_labels: Hides entities and devices with these labels.
data_description.excluded_loggers: Hides log records whose logger name contains this text, for example websocket_api.

data_description.enabled_tools: A tool you turn off cannot be called. Tools added by later versions stay off once you have saved this list.

data_description.allowed_services: A domain allows all its services, for example light. A service allows only that one, for example light.turn_on. * allows the services of every domain, except homeassistant and hassio. Automations and scripts written by a client are limited to these too, as they run later with all rights. Allowing something that runs other things, such as script, allows whatever those do. Domains homeassistant and hassio can only be allowed one service at a time. Some can never be allowed: shell commands, python scripts, stopping the system, and this integration itself.
data_description.protected_areas: A client can see these and what is in them, but not change them.
data_description.protected_domains: A client can see the entities of these domains, but not change them.
data_description.protected_entities: A client can see these entities, but not change them.
data_description.protected_integrations: A client can see these and what they provide, but not change them. This integration and the MCP server can never be changed.
data_description.protected_labels: A client can see what has these labels, but not change it.
data_description.write_allow_delete: Without this, a client can create and change things, but deleting is refused everywhere.
data_description.write_allow_templates: Warning: a template can read anything in Home Assistant, including the values withheld under Redaction, and a client can then read the result back from a trace or a state. With this on, redaction no longer protects what a client wants to get at. It has no effect while anything is hidden: templates stay refused then.
data_description.write_subjects: Nothing can be changed until you select something here. Each choice adds tools for clients.

writes.description: Clients can only read until you allow something here. A client cannot change these settings. Every change needs a reason and is recorded under recent activity.
